title: Feeble, Helpless, How Shall I
description: Feeble, Helpless, How Shall I in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Furness wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 214, “Christ Who Strengtheneth Me”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fee-ble, help-less, how shall I Learn to live and learn to die? Who, O God, my guide shall be? Who shall lead thy child to Thee?

lines: Feeble, helpless, how shall I
Learn to live and learn to die?
Who, O God, my guide shall be?
Who shall lead thy child to Thee?
Blessed Father, gracious One,
Thou hast sent thy holy Son;
He will give the light I need,
He my trembling steps will lead.
Through this world, uncertain, dim,
Let me ever learn of him;
From his precepts wisdom draw,
Make his life my solemn law.
Thus in deed, and thought, and word,
Led by Jesus Christ the Lord,
In my weakness, thus shall I
Learn to live and learn to die;
Learn to live in peace and love,
Like the perfect ones above; —
Learn to die without a fear,
Feeling Thee, my Father, near.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Henry Furness died in 1896.
credits: Words by William Henry Furness (1802–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
